cf.title: JSON_SERIALIZE for JSONB returns parts of the internal JSONB representation

input.subject: JSON_SERIALIZE for JSONB returns parts of the internal JSONB representation

verdict_reasoning: The bug is reproduced on master, the docs allow a jsonb argument, and no objection to fixing it survived. The two surviving objections, standards-compat-1 and replication-ondisk-1, are fixable and concern expressions already stored when the parser-only fix is backpatched through 17. A committer who knows the SQL/JSON parser code has to choose between the parser fix and an executor-side fix for back branches. No one but the author has replied yet.

brief.title: Fix JSON_SERIALIZE() returning jsonb header bytes for a jsonb argument
brief.problem: JSON_SERIALIZE() on a jsonb value returns a few bytes of the internal jsonb header, such as \x03 for '[1,2,4]'::jsonb, instead of the JSON text. The reporter saw it on 18.3; the patch author reproduced it on master. The output can also be text that is not valid in the server encoding.
brief.proposed_design: makeJsonConstructorExpr() built the output coercion for a json input because it took the input type from the RETURNING format, which is always JSON. The patch builds the coercion from the type of the argument instead, so json_out() no longer runs on jsonb data. The fix is in the parser, so stored expressions keep the old behaviour until recreated.
user_visible_surface: JSON_SERIALIZE() with a jsonb argument returns the JSON text instead of header bytes.
Views and other stored expressions that call JSON_SERIALIZE() on jsonb stay wrong until recreated.
author_claims: The docs allow any JSON type as the JSON_SERIALIZE() argument, so jsonb should work.
Converting in the executor would cover old views but adds a step and keeps the wrong coercion in the tree.
Casting jsonb to json in transformJsonSerializeExpr() works but converts twice.
The fix should be backpatched through 17.
brief.thread_state: The reporter posted in March; the patch author replied in September with v1 and rebased to v2 in November. No committer or other reviewer has replied.
unclear: The material does not say whether release notes will tell users to recreate affected views, or how they find them.
The material does not say whether other SQL/JSON constructors share the same coercion bug with jsonb input.
The material does not say whether any user relies on the current output, for example through RETURNING bytea.

objections.title: Parser-only fix leaves existing views wrong after a minor update
objections.failure_scenario: A user on 17 or 18 has a view that calls JSON_SERIALIZE() on a jsonb column. After the minor update the view still returns header bytes. A copy restored from pg_dump re-parses the view and returns JSON text, so the two servers give different results for the same view.
objections.argument: Message #2 and the 0001 commit message say stored expressions keep the old coercion until recreated, and the patch targets back branches through 17. A minor release is expected to fix bugs without user action, but a minor update does not re-parse stored rules. Message #2 rejects the executor-side fix because it adds a step and keeps the wrong coercion in the tree, but it is the only option that also fixes existing views. The proposal does not give release-note text or a query that finds affected views.
objections.author_must_show: How will users on 17 and 18 find and fix existing views after the minor update, or why is an executor-side fix for old trees not worth its cost?

critic.reasoning: Message #2 names the limitation and two alternatives, but it gives no way to find affected views and does not weigh the executor-side fix for back branches. A release note or a catalog query can close this, so fixable is the right severity.

objections.title: Expression indexes and stored generated columns keep old values after upgrade
objections.failure_scenario: A user has an expression index or a stored generated column on JSON_SERIALIZE(jsonb_col). pg_upgrade or dump and restore re-parses the expression with the fixed parser, but pg_upgrade copies the index files and table data unchanged. Index lookups with the new expression then miss rows, and generated column values no longer match their expression, with no error.
objections.argument: Message #2 and the commit message say the fix lives in the parser and that stored expressions must be recreated. Re-parsing happens silently whenever an expression is deparsed and restored, so the stored expression and the stored data can disagree after pg_upgrade. The proposal does not say whether JSON_SERIALIZE() on jsonb is accepted in index and generated column expressions. It gives no reindex or rewrite instruction.
objections.author_must_show: Can JSON_SERIALIZE() on jsonb appear in an index or stored generated column, and if so, what must users run after pg_upgrade or a minor update?

critic.reasoning: The material does not rule out JSON_SERIALIZE() on jsonb in an index or stored generated column, and pg_upgrade re-parses expressions while copying data files unchanged. A reindex or rewrite note would answer it, so it stays fixable.

refuted.title: Backpatched parser fix leaves existing views wrong with no way to find them
refuted.failure_scenario: A user on 17 installs the minor release with this fix. New queries return JSON text, but a view created earlier still returns jsonb header bytes, so the same expression gives two answers. A materialized view refreshed from the old view keeps writing text that may be invalid in the server encoding, and a later restore of that data can fail.
refuted.argument: The patch leaves wrong expressions in pg_rewrite and pg_attrdef after an in-place minor update (message #2). The executor-side alternative in message #2 would fix stored trees too, and message #2 rejects it only because it adds a step. In back branches that trade may favour the executor fix. The proposal gives no query to find affected objects and no release-note text.
refuted.author_must_show: For back branches, why is a parser-only fix better than also handling old stored trees, and how will users find the views, rules and defaults that need recreating?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. It also understates message #2, which rejects the executor-side fix for two reasons, the added step and the wrong coercion staying in the tree.

refuted.title: Parser-only fix leaves existing views returning header bytes after minor upgrade
refuted.failure_scenario: A site on 17 or 18 has a view that calls JSON_SERIALIZE() on a jsonb column. They install the minor release with this fix, and the view keeps returning header bytes without any error. They find out only when a consumer of the view fails, or when they read release notes they may never see.
refuted.argument: The commit message says stored expressions keep the old coercion until recreated, and it asks for a backpatch through 17. Message #2 rejects an executor-side conversion because it "adds a step" and keeps the wrong coercion in the tree. For a back-branch fix, a committer would likely weigh covering existing views above one extra check, because minor releases are not expected to require object recreation. The proposal does not say how users find affected views or what the release notes will tell them.
refuted.author_must_show: Why is a parser-only fix acceptable for back branches when existing views stay silently wrong, and how would users find the views they must recreate?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which states the same stored-view scenario and adds the pg_dump divergence case.

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows the SQL/JSON constructor code in the parser and executor, and the rules for backpatching fixes that affect stored expressions.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a behaviour change in 17 and 18 minor releases, for the release-note text, and for any reports about stored views, indexes or generated columns that stay wrong.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v1 in message #2 and a rebased v2 in message #3 about two months later, so the author is still following the patch.

priority.reason: A documented function returns jsonb header bytes, sometimes invalid in the server encoding, and the fix touches one parser file and adds tests. Only callers of JSON_SERIALIZE() with jsonb are affected, and the open point is the back-branch handling of stored expressions.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the review could not confirm that the new coercion is right for every RETURNING type. It also could not check whether other callers of makeJsonConstructorExpr() change behaviour.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add jsonb_translate(jsonb, from, to)
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andrew Dunstan, Pavel Stehule, Peter Eisentraut
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds jsonb_translate(jsonb, from, to), and in v2 json_translate, which recursively replaces every value, including array elements, that exactly equals a given string with another string. The author meant it for mapping categorical or enum values deep inside a document, in the style of the Unix tr utility.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andrew Dunstan judged blind replacement of every instance of a string, regardless of context, to be a niche use and asked why it could not be an extension. Pavel Stehule suggested using JsonPath to say what to replace, and Peter Eisentraut pointed to json_transform in Oracle and the SQL standard draft, noting that json_transform and json_translate together might confuse users. The thread ends there, and the author later withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Blindly replacing every
instance of a single string regardless of context seems at best a niche
use. Is there any reason not to make this an extension?

precedents_retrieved.title: Jsonb transform for pl/python
precedents_retrieved.summary: A set of extensions (jsonb_plpythonu, jsonb_plpython2u, jsonb_plpython3u) implementing a CREATE TRANSFORM for jsonb in PL/Python, mapping jsonb objects to dicts, arrays to lists, and numerics to Python Decimal via string conversion, and back. The transform works in both directions so functions can take and return jsonb as native Python values.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The reviewer objected that the third version turned unsupported Python objects such as set() into JSON strings instead of raising an error, asked for tests and errors for complex numbers and ranges, and reported that the tests failed on Python 3. The author sent no revised version after that review, and the commitfest manager returned the patch with feedback because it still needed work and had had no updates for more than a week.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So this still needs more work.. I am marking it as returned with
feedback as there has been no updates for more than 1 week.

precedents_retrieved.title: Optimize JsonbContainerTypeName by reordering type checks
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch reorders the checks in JsonbContainerTypeName() so that the array and object bit checks run before the scalar check. The author argued that this avoids calling JsonbExtractScalar() in most cases and reported about 0.8% higher tps for jsonb_typeof().
precedents_retrieved.objection: David Rowley argued that one function call cannot change the speed of a whole query by a measurable amount. His test called the function 1 million times and found the patch 3.5% slower, and perf top showed JsonbExtractScalar using little CPU time. Andreas Karlsson added that scalars are not clearly less common, so the new order would slow some workloads while it speeds up others.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It'll amount to a few dozen instructions for the function out of several 10s of millions, when you consider the cost of processing the entire query.

precedents_retrieved.title: Collecting statistics about contents of JSONB columns
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a jsonb_typanalyze function that extracts every path from sampled JSONB documents and stores per-path statistics as an array of JSONB documents in pg_statistic under a new stakind. It also adds an "oprstat" procedure for operators such as ->> so the planner can derive statistics for expressions on JSONB columns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tests showed ANALYZE becoming much slower: about 28 seconds against 120 ms on one data set, and over 2 hours or OOM on documents with about 850k distinct paths, because the patch loops over all sample rows once per path. The reviewers agreed the design of collecting statistics for every path in every JSONB column needs rethinking, for example by keeping only the most common paths or enabling the statistics per column. Nikita Glukhov posted optimizations and planned common-path collection, but in the last week of the commitfest the patch no longer applied and Greg Stark asked for a rebase.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: From these points, we can say that we should rethink our design to collect stats for all paths.

precedents_retrieved.title: jsonb array-style subscription
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add array-style subscripting to jsonb, so that values can be read with expressions like test_json['a']['a1'] and updated with assignments like UPDATE ... SET test_json['a']['a1']['a2'] = 42. The work-in-progress patch did this by extending the existing ArrayRef node, using the parser's hard-coded array subscript handling, to cover jsonb.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The early messages raise design concerns: using array syntax as key/value syntax, update assignments creating missing intermediate objects, and the lack of an operator that could use a GIN index. The visible messages end in August 2015 and the decision was in March 2016, so the shown text does not connect any of these concerns to the outcome.

precedents_retrieved.title: SERIALIZABLE on standby servers
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch allows SERIALIZABLE READ ONLY DEFERRABLE transactions on standby servers by having the primary write snapshot safety information into commit records and separate WAL records. The standby waits for a point in the WAL stream where a snapshot is known to be safe, using hypothetical transactions that the primary tracks as stand-ins for standby transactions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author called the patch prototype/WIP code with unsolved problems. Two of them are a race between the safety decision and the order of commit records in WAL, and the absence of snapshot safety information in checkpoints. A third is that the primary makes transactions visible in ProcArrayEndTransaction() order while the standby uses commit record order, which can allow serialization anomalies. No review of the general approach came, and the entry was later withdrawn; the visible messages do not show who withdrew it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: And that's precisely the issue: on the primary, transactions become visible to other transactions in the order in which they perform ProcArrayEndTransaction(), but on the standby, they become visible in the order in which they RecordTransactionCommit().

precedents_retrieved.title: WIP: Pgbench Errors and serialization/deadlock retries
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets pgbench clients keep running after serialization and deadlock failures instead of disconnecting, and reports these failures in progress output, logs and final reports. Later versions roll back and retry the failed script up to a configurable maximum number of tries.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last messages shown are a partial review by Fabien COELHO in August 2017 listing many open points, then a December 2017 reply from the author on some of them; the messages before the March 2018 decision are not shown.

precedents_retrieved.title: WIP: Pgbench Errors and serialization/deadlock retries
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets pgbench clients survive serialization and deadlock failures instead of disconnecting, retry the failed script as a transaction (controlled by --max-tries and --latency-limit), and report failures and retries in progress output, logs and the final report. Later versions split out preparatory patches for a RandomState structure, a Variables structure and a new error reporting function.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier returned the patch with feedback because Fabien COELHO's last reviews had stayed unanswered for a couple of weeks. The main open objection was that the v11 main patch also changed behavior for meta-command and other SQL errors: pgbench counted them as failures and kept looping instead of aborting with a clear message. Fabien asked that this change be removed and proposed separately. Smaller code and naming issues from his reviews were also still open.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I'm mostly saying that your patch should focus on implementing the retry feature when appropriate, and avoid changing the behavior (error displayed, abort or not) on features unrelated to serialization & deadlock errors.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P6] reverted the whole SQL/JSON feature set in 2022, and its record gives only the list of reverted commits, not a reason that applies to this parser fix for JSON_SERIALIZE() with a jsonb argument. The thread does not point to any earlier discussion of this bug or fix.
The fix matches the documented contract that any JSON type is accepted. The current output is header bytes, so no user should rely on it.
The fix adds no new WAL records, catalogs, wire messages or on-disk formats. The objections above are only about expressions already stored in catalogs and data built from them.

The patch adds no privilege, role or default, and gives no user access to anything they could not reach before. The bug only exposed header bytes of the caller's own jsonb value, and the fix removes that. One point a committer may still check: after a backpatched parser-only fix, views that already exist can keep returning text that is not valid in the server encoding. That is a correctness and encoding issue, not a privilege boundary, and other angles cover it.
Beyond the back-branch view issue, the fix is small, is confined to one parser file, and adds no hot-path cost, API or new surface to maintain.

The proposal fixes a bug, so no existing feature or extension meets the need. Casting the argument first (`json_serialize(x::json)`) or using `x::text` avoids the wrong output, but users who hit the bug cannot know to do that, and the docs say any JSON type is accepted. The precedent [P6] is the 2022 SQL/JSON revert and gives no reason that applies to this fix.

This is a bug fix for a documented function that returns jsonb header bytes, possibly invalid in the server encoding, instead of JSON text; a user reported it on 18.3. Correct output from a documented function needs no further proof of demand, and the cost falls only on callers of JSON_SERIALIZE() with jsonb.
